scopeReview: SPS-5.D.1–2: high-yield seed/input/management systems; production gains, human access/costs, resource balances and environmental effects. Distinguishes conventional breeding from an assumed transgenic requirement and conditional land sparing from guaranteed conservation.
varietyReview: Four assessed stimuli: controlled variety/input interaction, original access/adoption map, regional irrigation-expansion chart and whole-cost farm accounts. Fifth numerical check recomputes fixed-demand land requirements; application items cover biology, water quality, equity and balanced evaluation. Eleven original questions with all-option explanations and varied keys.
repetitionReview: Distinct units/denominators: t/ha treatment interaction, farm adoption percentage, regional withdrawals despite lower water/ha, net currency return and fixed-demand hectares. No literal or numeric-only clones of prior questions; broader gains/limits integrated rather than asserting a uniform historical outcome. Difficulty uncalibrated.
referenceNote: Primary research institutions verify broad variety/management and sustainability themes; original synthetic trial/account/water data are not copied institutional findings. No technical farm advice, paid API, new video/resource approval or independent human-review claim.

questions.correctOption: Its yield advantage is much greater with the supplied water-and-nutrient package than under low-input conditions.
questions.independentReview: Independently recomputed improved-minus-traditional advantages0.2 and2.0 t/ha and within-variety responses2.8 versus1.0. Trial explicitly controls other conditions; water and nutrients form a combined treatment, so their separate effects cannot be isolated.

questions.correctOption: Supporting infrastructure and finance may help explain uneven adoption, but the two-district comparison is not a complete causal test.
questions.independentReview: Verified map values80% and25%, a55-point gap; notes explicitly provide reliable irrigation/credit differences, not farm-size distributions. No climate, country-specific historical statistic or inevitable causal effect is invented.

questions.correctOption: It rises 25%; lower water use per hectare has not reduced total regional withdrawals.
questions.independentReview: Independently multiplied area by water/ha:10000×8000=80000000 and20000×5000=100000000m³; total growth25%, unit decline37.5%. Distinct from the earlier aquifer-balance item: this tests expansion offsetting efficiency, not recharge minus withdrawal or an exhaustion date.

questions.correctOption: It falls from 400 to 300 currency units even though physical output doubles.
questions.independentReview: Independently calculated revenues600/1200 and net returns400/300, a100-unit fall or25% decrease. Costs are explicitly all listed annual production costs; no hidden loan rate or invented external loss is required.

questions.correctOption: The spread of high-yield crop varieties with complementary inputs and management, including fertilizers, irrigation where needed and mechanization.
questions.independentReview: Cross-checked SPS-5.D.1’s high-yield seed, chemicals and mechanization; irrigation qualified rather than universally required for every improved variety or location.

questions.correctOption: Conventional crossing and selection can produce improved varieties without inserting genes through transgenic methods.
questions.independentReview: Checked that the claim is limited to distinguishing methods, not that no modern improved cultivar is engineered. The original Green Revolution is not defined by compulsory transgenic technology; no disputed event date is needed.

questions.correctOption: A shared susceptibility across many fields can make losses more correlated if that pathogen spreads.
questions.independentReview: Conditioned the conclusion on one specified shared disease susceptibility. Avoided equating all commercial seed with clones or asserting every traditional variety is resistant.

questions.correctOption: Nutrient enrichment can stimulate algal growth, and subsequent decomposition can reduce dissolved oxygen.
questions.independentReview: Verified nitrogen/phosphorus enrichment and decomposition oxygen-demand pathway, avoiding the misconception that all algal presence directly consumes all oxygen only during photosynthesis. No real lake data or agronomic prescription invented.

questions.correctOption: It falls from 3000 to 1200 hectares, a reduction of 1800 hectares.
questions.independentReview: Independently recomputed3000−1200=1800 hectares,60% below the original area. Tested all numeric alternatives against output=area×yield. Land sparing is conditional on fixed demand and no rebound or conversion change.

questions.correctOption: Net returns, debt exposure and water access separated by farm-size and income groups.
questions.independentReview: Selected evidence tied to the stated equity question rather than asserting a universal outcome by farm size. National output and household/farm accounts have different inferential scope.

questions.correctOption: Higher yields can strengthen food supplies while intensive input use may create water, pollution or access problems that require separate assessment.
questions.independentReview: Compared SPS-5.D.2’s positive and negative consequences with IRRI/CIMMYT research themes. Retained conditional language and separate outcome measures; no human-review, guaranteed sustainability or all-farmer-benefit claim.
